# montecarlo_azure_sql_database_credentials (Resource)

Azure SQL Database credentials are the login Monte Carlo stores for Azure SQL Database connections to use. The password is never returned.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An Azure SQL Database connection with credentials Monte Carlo stores: the
# warehouse, a database user and its password, and the connection that joins
# them.
#
# The warehouse type is taken from `connection_type`: Azure SQL Database
# connections live on a `transactional-db` warehouse.
#
# To keep the password in your own store instead, use one of the self-hosted
# credentials resources.
#
# See https://docs.getmontecarlo.com/docs/azure-sql-database for creating the
# user and granting it the reads Monte Carlo needs.

terraform {
  # Write-only arguments need Terraform 1.11 or later.
  required_version = ">= 1.11"

  required_providers {
    montecarlo = {
      source = "monte-carlo-data/montecarlo"
    }
  }
}

provider "montecarlo" {
  # Credentials come from the environment or from the Monte Carlo CLI's profile.
  # See the provider documentation for the alternatives.
}

# The `montecarlo_warehouse` example shows the deployment and agent behind
# `deployment_id`.
resource "montecarlo_warehouse" "azure_sql_database" {
  name            = "production-azure-sql-database"
  connection_type = "azure-sql-database"
  deployment_id   = "<deployment id, from the Monte Carlo app>"
}

resource "montecarlo_azure_sql_database_credentials" "azure_sql_database" {
  host    = "example-server.database.windows.net"
  port    = 1433
  db_name = "analytics"
  user    = "monte_carlo"

  # In a real configuration, pass the password from a sensitive variable or a
  # secret store rather than a literal in a committed file.
  #
  # Write-only, so never stored in state or a plan. Changing it alone plans
  # nothing: bump the version with it.
  password_wo         = "..."
  password_wo_version = 1
}

# The connection's type comes from the credentials, and has to fit the
# warehouse's type.
resource "montecarlo_connection" "azure_sql_database" {
  name           = "production-azure-sql-database"
  warehouse_id   = montecarlo_warehouse.azure_sql_database.id
  credentials_id = montecarlo_azure_sql_database_credentials.azure_sql_database.id
}

output "connection_id" {
  description = "Id of the connection."
  value       = montecarlo_connection.azure_sql_database.id
}

output "connection_type" {
  description = "What the connection reaches, taken from the credentials."
  value       = montecarlo_connection.azure_sql_database.connection_type
}
```

## Schema

### Required

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `db_name` (String) Database to connect to.
- `host` (String) Hostname of the database endpoint.
- `password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Password of the database user. Stored by Monte Carlo and never returned.
- `password_wo_version` (Number) Bump to send `password_wo` again. Terraform stores this, never the secret.
- `port` (Number) Port the database listens on.
- `user` (String) Database user Monte Carlo logs in as.

### Read-Only

- `connection_type` (String) The connection type the credentials are for, such as `snowflake`. Fixed once created.
- `created_time` (String) When the credentials were created.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier of the credentials.
- `storage_type` (String) Where the secret lives. Fixed once created.
